items.label: Setup S-1
items.nl: A randomized binary trial on \(d\ge2\) public strata with \(n\ge2\) participants. A full-data law \(P\in\mathcal P_d\) is a probability law of \((X,A,Y,Y^0,Y^1)\) on \([d]\times\{0,1\}^4\); the observed record is \(O=(X,A,Y)\in\mathcal O=[d]\times\{0,1\}^2\) with law \(P_O\), and the sample is \(\mathbf O\sim P_O^{\otimes n}\). The class \(\mathcal V_d\) requires \(P(X=j)=1/d\), fair assignment independent of \((X,Y^0,Y^1)\), consistency \(Y=Y^{\mathrm{pot}}_A\), and arm means \(\mu_{aj}(P)=\mathbb E_P[Y^{\mathrm{pot}}_a\mid X=j]\in[1/4,3/4]\). With \(\tau_j=\mu_{1j}-\mu_{0j}\), \(B(P)=\mathbb E_P[Y]\), and \(S=(2A-1)(2Y-1)\), the target is \(V(P)=d^{-1}\sum_j\max\{\mu_{0j},\mu_{1j}\}\). For \(\theta\in[-1/2,1/2]^d\), \(P_\theta(j,s)=(1+s\theta_j)/(2d)\) on \([d]\times\{-1,1\}\), \(\mathsf U_{2d}\) is the uniform law there, \(F(\theta)=d^{-1}\sum_j|\theta_j|\), and \(G_\theta\) is the symmetric causal law with arm means \((1\mp\theta_j)/2\).

items.label: Setup S-2
items.nl: Pure local differential privacy with public budget \(\varepsilon\in(0,1]\). A protocol consists of a standard-Borel public-seed space \(\mathcal R\) with law \(\lambda\), standard-Borel message spaces \((\mathcal Z_i)_{i\le n}\) with histories \(\mathcal H_i=\prod_{\ell<i}\mathcal Z_\ell\), and one-message Markov kernels \(Q_i\) from \(\mathcal O\times\mathcal H_i\times\mathcal R\) to \(\mathcal Z_i\) with \(Q_i(E\mid o,\eta,r)\le e^\varepsilon Q_i(E\mid o',\eta,r)\) for all arguments (class \(\mathfrak Q_{\mathrm{SI}}\)); \(\mathfrak Q_{\mathrm{NI}}\) additionally requires constancy in the history. The seed \(R\sim\lambda\) and the analyst randomizer \(U\sim\operatorname{Uniform}[0,1]\) are independent of each other and of \(\mathbf O\); \(\mathbf Z\) is the transcript. Decisions are Borel estimators \(T(\mathbf Z,R,U)\) and connected closed intervals \(I(\mathbf Z,R,U)\subseteq[1/4,3/4]\) with ordered Borel endpoints. \(\mathfrak R_{\mathcal C}\) is the minimax squared-error risk and \(\mathfrak H_{\mathcal C}\) the minimax worst-law expected length under global coverage \(0.90\), for \(\mathcal C\in\{\mathrm{NI},\mathrm{SI}\}\). The rate is \(r_{\mathcal C}=\rho(n\varepsilon^2,d)\) and \(h_{\mathcal C}=\sqrt{r_{\mathcal C}}\), compared up to universal constants \(0<c\le C_0\).

items.label: Setup S-3
items.nl:
Converse objects for a sequential protocol \(Q\): \( eta=(e^\varepsilon-1)/(2d)\); probability measures \(
u_0,
u_1\) on \([-\alpha,\alpha]\), \(\alpha\in(0,1/2]\), with equal moments \(\int u^q\,d
u_0=\int u^q\,d
u_1\) for \(q<k\); product priors \(\Pi_l=
u_l^{\otimes d}\); mixture laws \(\mathsf M_l^Q\) of \((R,\mathbf Z)\) when \(	heta\sim\Pi_l\) and records follow \(G_	heta\); the reference transcript law \(\Lambda_r^Q\) under \(G_0\) at seed \(r\); and the transcript density \(p^Q(	heta,r)=d\mathcal L_{G_	heta,Q}(\mathbf Z\mid R=r)/d\Lambda_r^Q\).

items.label: Setup S-4
items.nl: Attaining construction: \(\delta=\tanh(\varepsilon/2)\), \(b=d/\delta\); the signed-vector channel \(Q^{\mathrm{vec}}(z\mid(j,A,Y))=2^{-d}(1+\delta S z_j)\) on \(z\in\{-1,1\}^d\); for a block of \(m\le n\) participants, messages \(Z^{\mathrm{vec}}_i\), scaled entries \(W_{ij}=bZ^{\mathrm{vec}}_{ij}\), and distinct-person moments \(\mathsf U_{kj}=\binom mk^{-1}\sum_{|J|=k}\prod_{i\in J}W_{ij}\); column statistics \(T^{\mathrm{col}}_j=g_j(W_{1j},\ldots,W_{mj})\) for deterministic \(g_j\).

items.label: Setup S-5
items.nl: Paired total-variation models on \(\mathcal A_d=[d]\times\{-1,1\}\): the simplex \(\Delta_{2d}\) of all probability laws \(\mathsf p\), the paired family \(\mathcal P_d^{\mathrm{pair}}=\{P_\theta:\theta\in[-1/2,1/2]^d\}\), and the target \(D_{\mathrm{TV}}(\mathsf p)=\tfrac12\sum_{j,s}|\mathsf p(j,s)-1/(2d)|\). For a model \(\mathcal M\) among these two, data are \(n\) iid draws from \(\mathsf p\in\mathcal M\); protocols \(\mathsf K\in\mathfrak K_{\mathcal C}\) are the same one-message pure-local NI/SI classes with input alphabet \(\mathcal A_d\), transcript \(\mathbf Z^{\mathsf K}\), estimators \(\widehat D\) and connected closed intervals \(J_{\mathrm{TV}}\subseteq[0,1]\), with minimax values \(\mathfrak R^{\mathrm{TV}}_{\mathcal C}(\mathcal M;n,d,\varepsilon)\) and \(\mathfrak H^{\mathrm{TV}}_{\mathcal C}(\mathcal M;n,d,\varepsilon)\).

items.label: Definition P-2
items.nl: \(\mathfrak Q_{\mathrm{SI}}(n,d,\varepsilon)=\{Q=(Q_i)_{i=1}^n:\ Q_i\text{ are the declared Markov kernels and }Q_i(E\mid o,\eta,r)\le e^\varepsilon Q_i(E\mid o\prime,\eta,r)\text{ for every }i,o,o\prime,\eta,r,E\}\)

items.label: Definition P-3
items.nl: \(\mathfrak Q_{\mathrm{NI}}(n,d,\varepsilon)=\{Q\in\mathfrak Q_{\mathrm{SI}}(n,d,\varepsilon):\ Q_i(\cdot\mid o,\eta,r)\text{ is constant in }\eta\text{ for every }i,o,r\}\)

items.label: Definition P-4
items.nl: \(\mathfrak R_{\mathcal C}(n,d,\varepsilon)=\inf_{Q\in\mathfrak Q_{\mathcal C}(n,d,\varepsilon)}\inf_T\sup_{P\in\mathcal V_d}\mathbb E_{P,Q}[(T(\mathbf Z,R,U)-V(P))^2]\). Here \(\mathfrak Q_{\mathcal C}\) selects the declared NI or SI class.

items.label: Definition P-5
items.nl: \(\mathfrak H_{\mathcal C}(n,d,\varepsilon)=\inf_{Q\in\mathfrak Q_{\mathcal C}(n,d,\varepsilon)}\ \inf_{I:\inf_{P\in\mathcal V_d}\Pr_{P,Q}\{V(P)\in I(\mathbf Z,R,U)\}\ge0.90}\ \sup_{P\in\mathcal V_d}\mathbb E_{P,Q}[\operatorname{length}I(\mathbf Z,R,U)]\). The second infimum ranges over the declared Borel connected closed interval decisions.

items.label: Definition P-6
items.nl: Generate \(X\sim\operatorname{Uniform}[d]\); given \(X=j\), generate conditionally independent \(Y^0\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}((1-\theta_j)/2)\) and \(Y^1\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}((1+\theta_j)/2)\); generate independent \(A\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/2)\) and set \(Y=Y^{\mathrm{pot}}_A\). The resulting full-data law is \(G_\theta\).

items.label: Definition P-7
items.nl: \(Q^{\mathrm{vec}}(z\mid O=(j,A,Y))=2^{-d}(1+\delta(2A-1)(2Y-1)z_j)\). A total sampler draws all coordinates except \(j\) fairly and draws coordinate \(j\) with sign mean \(\delta S\).

items.label: Definition P-8
items.nl: \(\mathsf U_{kj}=\binom{m}{k}^{-1}\sum_{J\subseteq\{1,\ldots,m\}:|J|=k}\prod_{i\in J}W_{ij}\quad(1\le k\le m),\qquad\mathsf U_{0j}=1\). The subset \(J\) is bound by the displayed sum. Elementary-symmetric recursions compute these quantities without enumerating subsets.

items.label: Definition P-9
items.nl:
Define \(\mathscr H\) to be the following fixed public-resource construction for estimating \(V(P)\). Every auxiliary introduced in this construction, including its summation indices, is locally bound. Fix
\[
 \eta_*=\frac1{1024},\qquad L_0=4096,
 \qquad t=n\varepsilon^2,\qquad L=\log(ed),
 \qquad z_*=\frac{d^2L}{t},\qquad w=\log(e+z_*).
\]
Define the numerical auxiliary
\[
 \rho(t,d)=
 \begin{cases}
 \displaystyle\frac{d^2}{tL},&t\ge d^2L,\\[3pt]
 \displaystyle\min\left\{1,
       \left[\frac{\log(e+d^2L/t)}{L}\right]^2\right\},
       &0<t<d^2L.
 \end{cases}
\]
Use a singleton public seed and ignore analyst randomization. If \(n=2\), each participant sends a constant message and set \(\widehat V=1/2\); no block size or noise scale is used for this estimator branch.

If \(n>2\), set \(m=\lfloor n/3\rfloor\) and \(m_0=n-2m\). In the fixed participant order, use a fresh baseline block of size \(m_0\), a disjoint signed-vector pilot block of size \(m\), and a disjoint signed-vector evaluation block of size \(m\). The baseline participant's binary message \(\mathsf H_i\) has probabilities
\[
 \Pr(\mathsf H_i=h\mid O)
       =\frac{1+h\delta(2Y-1)}2,\qquad h\in\{-1,1\},
 \qquad
 \widehat B=\frac12+\frac1{2\delta m_0}
                  \sum_{i=1}^{m_0}\mathsf H_i.
\]
Here \(i\) indexes this block locally. For each participant in either vector block, apply exactly \(Q^{\mathrm{vec}}\) from \(\texttt{def:vector-kernel}\), once, with independent local randomness. Thus this is one fixed noninteractive original-input protocol used for both \(\mathfrak Q_{\mathrm{NI}}\) and \(\mathfrak Q_{\mathrm{SI}}\), with predetermined binary and sign-vector message alphabets.

Use the core scales \(\delta\) and \(b\). Write \(W^{\mathrm{pil}}\) and \(W^{\mathrm{ev}}\) for the two block instances of the scaled-message matrix \(W\), and set
\[
 \sigma^2=\frac{b^2}{m},\qquad \sigma=\sqrt{b^2/m},
 \qquad H=\log(e+\sigma^2L),
 \qquad M_j=\frac1m\sum_{i=1}^m W^{\mathrm{pil}}_{ij},
 \qquad \overline W_j=\frac1m\sum_{i=1}^m W^{\mathrm{ev}}_{ij}
       \quad(1\le j\le d).
\]
All uses of \(\mathsf U_{vj}\) below mean the evaluation-block moments from \(\texttt{def:private-moments}\); its elementary-symmetric recursion is the prescribed finite computation.

For each even degree \(D\ge2\) used below, let \(p_D^{\mathrm{abs}}\) be the explicit polynomial of \(\texttt{lem:cai-low-chebyshev-approximation}\), written with local notation as
\[
 \mathcal T_0(x)=1,\qquad \mathcal T_1(x)=x,\qquad
 \mathcal T_{v+1}(x)=2x\mathcal T_v(x)-\mathcal T_{v-1}(x),
\]
\[
 p_D^{\mathrm{abs}}(x)
   =\frac2\pi+\frac4\pi\sum_{v=1}^{D/2}
          \frac{(-1)^{v+1}\mathcal T_{2v}(x)}{4v^2-1}
   =\sum_{v=0}^D c_{D,v}x^v.
\]
For the positive local radius \(a_{\mathrm{rad}}\) specified in the selected branch, use the corresponding evaluation statistic
\[
 \widehat p_{a_{\mathrm{rad}},D,j}
       =\sum_{v=0}^D c_{D,v}a_{\mathrm{rad}}^{\,1-v}
                              \mathsf U_{vj}.
\]
These are the same polynomial and moment constructions as in \(\texttt{lem:finite-private-polynomial-calibration}\), with a distinct bound notation for the radius.

For \(n>2\), define the estimate \(\widehat F\) of \(F(\tau(P))\) by the following four ordered branches, taking the first applicable branch.

If \(L<L_0\), use the absolute evaluation means:
\[
 \widehat F=\frac1d\sum_{j=1}^d|\overline W_j|.
\]
Otherwise, if \(d^2L\le t\), use the hybrid construction with
\[
 D=2\left\lfloor\frac{L}{2048}\right\rfloor,
 \qquad T_*=4\sigma\sqrt L,
 \qquad a_{\mathrm{rad}}=8\sigma\sqrt L,
\]
\[
 \widehat F=\frac1d\sum_{j=1}^d
   \left[
     \widehat p_{a_{\mathrm{rad}},D,j}
           \mathbf1_{\{|M_j|\le T_*\}}
     +\operatorname{sign}(M_j)\overline W_j
           \mathbf1_{\{|M_j|>T_*\}}
   \right],\qquad \operatorname{sign}(0)=0.
\]
Otherwise, if \(L/(1024H)<4\), set \(\widehat F=1/4\). Otherwise, use the global polynomial construction:
\[
 a_{\mathrm{rad}}=\frac12,
 \qquad D=2\left\lfloor\frac{L}{2048H}\right\rfloor,
 \qquad \widehat F=\frac1d\sum_{j=1}^d
                           \widehat p_{a_{\mathrm{rad}},D,j}.
\]
For all these \(n>2\) branches, combine the baseline estimate of \(B(P)\) and the signed-norm estimate by
\[
 \widetilde V=\widehat B+\frac12\widehat F,
 \qquad
 \widehat V=\max\{1/4,\min\{3/4,\widetilde V\}\}.
\]
For every \(n\ge2\), including the constant-decision branch, set
\[
 q_*=\sqrt{10^{17}\rho(t,d)}
\]
and report the connected interval
\[
 [\max\{1/4,\widehat V-q_*\},
   \min\{3/4,\widehat V+q_*\}].
\]
The vector-channel admissibility and moment facts are those already established in \(\texttt{lem:private-moment-and-dependence}\), and the global and hybrid polynomial calibration is that of \(\texttt{lem:finite-private-polynomial-calibration}\). Risk and coverage for the combined decision are later consequences of this fixed construction.

The converse part of this same handle uses the following fixed local amplitude and integer degrees for every allowed resource tuple:
\[
 (\alpha,k)=
 \begin{cases}
 \left(\displaystyle\frac1{100}\sqrt{z_*},\,
                      2\lceil16L\rceil+1\right),&z_*\le1,\\[3pt]
 \left(\displaystyle\frac1{100},\,
                      2\lceil16L/w\rceil+1\right),&z_*>1,
 \end{cases}
 \qquad K=k-1.
\]
Use these amplitude and degree values in the scaled symmetric moment-matching measures supplied by \(\texttt{lem:cai-low-moment-duality}\), their independent coordinate product priors, and the causal laws \(G_\theta\) from \(\texttt{def:symmetric-law}\). Their original-record admissibility is established by \(\texttt{prop:signed-causal-bridge}\); the transcript contraction and decision reductions are the existing \(\texttt{lem:adaptive-moment-contraction}\), \(\texttt{lem:separated-value-mixtures}\), and \(\texttt{lem:dimension-free-private-two-point}\). This handle specifies the fixed resource choices and constructions, with no optimization over designs or interactive comparison program.

items.label: Definition P-10
items.nl:
Define the finite paired alphabet and its probability simplex by
\[
 \mathcal A_d=[d]\times\{-1,1\},\qquad
 \Delta_{2d}=\left\{\mathsf p:\mathcal A_d\to[0,1]:
          \sum_{j=1}^d\sum_{s\in\{-1,1\}}\mathsf p(j,s)=1\right\}.
\]
Here \(\mathsf p\) denotes a probability law on this alphabet, rather than a full-data causal law. Define
\[
 \mathcal P_d^{\mathrm{pair}}
   =\{P_\theta:\theta\in[-1/2,1/2]^d\}\subseteq\Delta_{2d},
 \qquad
 D_{\mathrm{TV}}(\mathsf p)=\frac12\sum_{j=1}^d\sum_{s\in\{-1,1\}}
                   \left|\mathsf p(j,s)-\frac1{2d}\right|.
\]
The reference law is the public \(\mathsf U_{2d}\). The two statistical models used below are \(\mathcal M=\mathcal P_d^{\mathrm{pair}}\) and \(\mathcal M=\Delta_{2d}\); their data consist of \(n\) iid draws from an unknown single member \(\mathsf p\). These definitions introduce a statistical corollary model and do not replace \(\mathcal V_d\) or its causal target.

items.label: Definition P-11
Assumption A-7
items.nl: \(Q_i(E\mid o,\eta,r)\le e^\varepsilon Q_i(E\mid o\prime,\eta,r)\) for every \(i,o,o\prime,\eta,r,E\) in their declared domains.

items.label: Assumption A-8
items.nl: \(Q_i(\cdot\mid o,\eta,r)=Q_i(\cdot\mid o,\eta\prime,r)\) for all histories \(\eta,\eta\prime\in\mathcal H_i\); \(\eta\prime\) is a second bound history argument.

items.label: Lemma L-1
items.nl: For every \(Q\in\mathfrak Q_{\mathrm{SI}}(n,d,\varepsilon)\) there are jointly measurable density versions such that, for every \(\theta,r,j\) and \(1\le k\le n\), \(\|\partial_{\theta_j}^{\,k}p^Q(\theta,r)\|_1\le k!\sqrt{\binom nk}\,\beta^k\); derivatives of order \(k>n\) vanish. If \(\int u^q\,d\nu_0(u)=\int u^q\,d\nu_1(u)\) for \(q=0,\ldots,k-1\), then \(\operatorname{TV}(\mathsf M_0^Q,\mathsf M_1^Q)\le\min\{1,d\alpha^k\sqrt{\binom nk}\,\beta^k\}\) for \(1\le k\le n\); the two mixture laws coincide when \(k>n\). The priors are fixed independently of \(R\); the claim integrates arbitrary public seeds and permits arbitrary Borel randomized transcript decisions.

items.label: Lemma L-2
items.nl: \(Q^{\mathrm{vec}}\in\mathfrak Q_{\mathrm{NI}}\) when applied once per participant. For every \(P\in\mathcal V_d\) its scaled messages for \(1\le i\le m\) satisfy \(\mathbb E[W_{ij}]=\tau_j(P)\), \(\mathbb E[W_{ij}^2]=b^2\) and \(\mathbb E[W_{ij}W_{ij\prime}]=0\) for \(j\ne j\prime\). For \(0\le k\le m\), \(\mathbb E[\mathsf U_{kj}]=\tau_j(P)^k\); for \(m\ge2k\), \(\mathbb E[\mathsf U_{kj}^2]\le(\tau_j(P)^2+2kb^2/m)^k\). For arbitrary declared deterministic column statistics, \(|\operatorname{Cov}(T_j^{\mathrm{col}},T_{j\prime}^{\mathrm{col}})|\le\frac{|\tau_j(P)\tau_{j\prime}(P)|}{\sqrt{(b^2-\tau_j(P)^2)(b^2-\tau_{j\prime}(P)^2)}}\sqrt{\operatorname{Var}(T_j^{\mathrm{col}})\operatorname{Var}(T_{j\prime}^{\mathrm{col}})}\) for \(j\ne j\prime\), and \(\operatorname{Var}(d^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^d T_j^{\mathrm{col}})\le(2/d)\max_{j\in[d]}\operatorname{Var}(T_j^{\mathrm{col}})\).

items.label: Lemma L-3
items.nl:
Fix a protocol \(Q\) and two probability priors supported on \(\mathcal V_d\), with joint seed/transcript mixture laws \(N_0,N_1\). Let their target centers be \(v_0<v_1\), with \(\Delta=v_1-v_0\). Suppose each prior gives \(\Pr\{|V-v_l|>\Delta/8\}\le\eta_0\), and \(\operatorname{TV}(N_0,N_1)\le\omega\). Every randomized transcript estimate satisfies
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal V_d}\mathbb E_{P,Q}(T-V(P))^2
 \ge\frac{9\Delta^2}{128}(1-\omega-2\eta_0)_+.
\]
Every connected interval with the declared finite global coverage satisfies
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal V_d}\mathbb E_{P,Q}\operatorname{length}I
 \ge\frac{3\Delta}{4}(0.80-2\eta_0-\omega)_+.
\]

items.label: Lemma L-4
items.nl:
There is a universal \(c_1>0\) such that for every allowed resource tuple and either \(\mathcal C\),
\[
 \mathfrak R_{\mathcal C}(n,d,\varepsilon)\ge c_1\min\{1,(n\varepsilon^2)^{-1}\},\qquad
 \mathfrak H_{\mathcal C}(n,d,\varepsilon)\ge c_1\min\{1,(\sqrt n\varepsilon)^{-1}\}.
\]

items.label: Lemma L-5
items.nl:
Set \(L=\log(ed)\), \(\eta_*=1/1024\), and \(\sigma^2=b^2/m\). For even \(D\ge2\), use the cited explicit Chebyshev polynomial \(q_D(x)=\sum_{v=0}^D a_{Dv}x^v\), and define
\[
 p_{a,D}(x)=a q_D(x/a),\qquad \widehat p_{a,D,j}=\sum_{v=0}^D a_{Dv}a^{1-v}\mathsf U_{vj}.
\]
For every \(P\in\mathcal V_d\) the following finite assertions hold. If \(m\ge2D\), \(H=\log(e+\sigma^2L)\), \(a=1/2\), and \(D\le\eta_*L/H\), then
\[
 |\mathbb E\widehat p_{a,D,j}-|\tau_j(P)||\le\frac1{D+1},\qquad
 \operatorname{Var}\left(d^{-1}\sum_j\widehat p_{a,D,j}\right)\le\frac{e^{9DH}}{2d}.
\]
If \(L\ge4096\), \(D=2\lfloor\eta_*L/2\rfloor\), \(m\ge2D\), and \(2m\le n\), take two independent blocks of \(m\) signed-vector releases. Let \(M_j\) be the scaled pilot mean and \(\overline W_j\) the evaluation mean, and use evaluation moments in \(\widehat p\). Put \(T_*=4\sigma\sqrt L\), \(a=2T_*\), and
\[
 H_j=\widehat p_{a,D,j}\mathbf1_{\{|M_j|\le T_*\}}+\operatorname{sign}(M_j)\overline W_j\mathbf1_{\{|M_j|>T_*\}}.
\]
Then
\[
 |\mathbb EH_j-|\tau_j(P)||\le20000\sigma/\sqrt L,\qquad
 \operatorname{Var}(H_j)\le400\sigma^2L e^{L/100},
\]
\[
 \mathbb E\left(d^{-1}\sum_jH_j-F(\tau(P))\right)^2\le5\cdot10^8\frac{\sigma^2}{L}.
\]
This includes ties, both sides of the pilot threshold, and all relative sizes of \(a\) and \(1/2\).

items.label: Theorem T-1
items.nl: For every \(P\in\mathcal V_d\), \(\mathbb E_P[S\mid X=j]=\tau_j(P)\), \(\mathcal L_P(X,S)=P_{\tau(P)}\) and \(V(P)=B(P)+F(\tau(P))/2=B(P)+\operatorname{TV}(P_{\tau(P)},\mathsf U_{2d})\). For every \(\theta\in[-1/2,1/2]^d\), \(G_\theta\in\mathcal V_d\) and \(V(G_\theta)=1/2+F(\theta)/2\). Under \(G_\theta\), conditional on \((X,S)\), \(A\) is an ancillary independent fair bit and \(2Y-1=S(2A-1)\). Integrating that bit from any original-record channel preserves its pure privacy inequality at every history and seed; deterministic preprocessing in the reverse direction does likewise. Thus the symmetric-subclass private experiments are equivalent in both declared protocol classes.

items.label: Theorem T-2
items.nl: There are \(0<c\le C_0<\infty\) such that for every \(n\ge2,\ \varepsilon\in(0,1],\ \mathcal C\in\{\mathrm{NI},\mathrm{SI}\}\), \(c\min\{1,(n\varepsilon^2)^{-1}\}\le\mathfrak R_{\mathcal C}(n,2,\varepsilon)\le C_0\min\{1,(n\varepsilon^2)^{-1}\}\) and \(c\min\{1,(\sqrt n\varepsilon)^{-1}\}\le\mathfrak H_{\mathcal C}(n,2,\varepsilon)\le C_0\min\{1,(\sqrt n\varepsilon)^{-1}\}\). Total NI original-record mechanisms and transcript estimators attain the risk upper bound; connected intervals contained in \([1/4,3/4]\) attain the length upper bound with finite global coverage at least \(0.90\).

items.label: Theorem T-3
items.nl:
Let \(t=n\varepsilon^2\) and \(L=\log(ed)\). For both \(\mathcal C\in\{\mathrm{NI},\mathrm{SI}\}\), set
\[
 r_{\mathcal C}(n,d,\varepsilon)=\rho(t,d)=
 \begin{cases}
 d^2/(tL),&t\ge d^2L,\\
 \min\{1,[\log(e+d^2L/t)/L]^2\},&0<t<d^2L,
 \end{cases}\qquad h_{\mathcal C}(n,d,\varepsilon)=\sqrt{\rho(t,d)}.
\]
There are universal \(0<c\le C_0<\infty\) such that for every allowed finite resource tuple and either class,
\[
 c r_{\mathcal C}\le\mathfrak R_{\mathcal C}\le C_0r_{\mathcal C},\qquad
 c h_{\mathcal C}\le\mathfrak H_{\mathcal C}\le C_0h_{\mathcal C}.
\]
Total explicit original-input noninteractive protocols with binary and finite sign-vector messages attain the upper orders, using transcript-only estimates and connected closed intervals in \([1/4,3/4]\) with globally finite \(0.90\) coverage. The converses cover every declared sequential channel, arbitrary shared independent seeds, standard-Borel outputs, nonidentical kernels, and adaptive histories. Thus both NI/SI minimax ratios lie between one and universal finite constants, and honest length has order square-root minimax risk.

The saturated branch is exactly \(t\le d^2L/(ed-e)\), the intermediate branch ends at \(d^2L\), and the dense branch starts there. Along arbitrary sequences of allowed tuples, risk and honest length vanish if and only if
\[
 t\to\infty,\qquad \frac{\log(1+d^2/t)}{\log(ed)}\to0.
\]
Along sequences with \(t\to\infty\), risk is of private-parametric order \(t^{-1}\) if and only if \(d\) stays bounded. More generally, comparability to \(t^{-1}\) along any sequence holds exactly when \(t\) is eventually bounded away from zero and \(\min\{t,d\}\) is eventually bounded above. At \(t\asymp d^2\), growing \(d\) gives risk order \([\log\log(ed)/\log(ed)]^2\).

items.label: Theorem lem:measurable-kernel-radon-nikodym
items.nl: Let \(H\) be a measurable space and \(Z\) a standard-Borel space. For finite kernels \(K,L:H\to Z\) satisfying \(K(h,\cdot)\ll L(h,\cdot)\) for every \(h\), there is a jointly measurable \(f:H\times Z\to[0,\infty]\) with \(K(h,E)=\int_E f(h,z)L(h,dz)\) for every \(h\) and measurable \(E\).

items.label: Theorem lem:bounded-mean-concentration
items.nl:
For independent real random variables \(H_1,\ldots,H_m\) supported on \([-b,b]\), and every \(x\ge0\),
\[
 \Pr\left\{m^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^m(H_i-\mathbb EH_i)\ge x\right\}\le e^{-mx^2/(2b^2)}.
\]
The same bound holds for the lower tail; adding them bounds the two-sided tail.

items.label: Theorem lem:cai-low-chebyshev-approximation
items.nl:
For even \(D\ge2\), define \(\mathcal T_0(x)=1\), \(\mathcal T_1(x)=x\), \(\mathcal T_{v+1}(x)=2x\mathcal T_v(x)-\mathcal T_{v-1}(x)\), and
\[
 q_D(x)=\frac2\pi+\frac4\pi\sum_{v=1}^{D/2}\frac{(-1)^{v+1}\mathcal T_{2v}(x)}{4v^2-1}
       =\sum_{v=0}^D a_{Dv}x^v.
\]
Then \(\sup_{|x|\le1}|q_D(x)-|x||\le2/[\pi(D+1)]\), and \(|a_{Dv}|\le2^{3D/2}\).

items.label: Theorem lem:cai-low-moment-duality
items.nl:
For every positive even integer \(K\), two symmetric probability measures \(\xi_0,\xi_1\) on \([-1,1]\) have equal moments through degree \(K\) and satisfy
\[
 \int|x|\,d\xi_1-\int|x|\,d\xi_0=2e_K,
 \qquad e_K=\inf_{\deg p\le K}\sup_{|x|\le1}|p(x)-|x||.
\]

items.label: Theorem T-4
items.nl:
Corollary (paired-uniform total-variation frontier). On the paired family
\[
 P_\theta(j,s)=\frac{1+s\theta_j}{2d},\qquad
 \theta\in[-1/2,1/2]^d,
 \qquad D_{\mathrm{TV}}(P_\theta)
     =\operatorname{TV}(P_\theta,\mathsf U_{2d})=\frac12F(\theta),
\]
there are universal \(0<c\le C_0<\infty\) such that, for every \(n\ge2\), \(d\ge2\), \(0<\varepsilon\le1\) and either \(\mathcal C\in\{\mathrm{NI},\mathrm{SI}\}\),
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 c\,r_{\mathcal C}(n,d,\varepsilon)
 &\le\mathfrak R^{\mathrm{TV}}_{\mathcal C}
           (\mathcal P_d^{\mathrm{pair}};n,d,\varepsilon)
       \le C_0\,r_{\mathcal C}(n,d,\varepsilon),\\
 c\,h_{\mathcal C}(n,d,\varepsilon)
 &\le\mathfrak H^{\mathrm{TV}}_{\mathcal C}
           (\mathcal P_d^{\mathrm{pair}};n,d,\varepsilon)
       \le C_0\,h_{\mathcal C}(n,d,\varepsilon).
 \end{aligned}
\]
The numerical functions are exactly the evaluated \(\rho(n\varepsilon^2,d)\) and its square root from the uniform private-value theorem. Total finite sign-vector NI channels, transcript polynomial estimates, and connected intervals contained in \([0,1/4]\) attain the upper orders with finite global \(0.90\) honesty. The converse is against every SI channel with arbitrary shared independent public seeds and standard-Borel outputs. Hence NI and SI have the same orders on this family, and the saturation, consistency, private-parametric and \(n\varepsilon^2\asymp d^2\) conclusions of that theorem also hold for these TV minimax quantities.

items.label: Theorem T-5
items.nl:
Corollary (full-simplex total-variation converse). On the arbitrary \(2d\)-symbol simplex \(\Delta_{2d}\), with iid private inputs and the same one-person-one-message pure-local protocol classes, there is a universal \(c>0\) such that, for every \(n\ge2\), \(d\ge2\), \(0<\varepsilon\le1\) and either \(\mathcal C\in\{\mathrm{NI},\mathrm{SI}\}\),
\[
 \mathfrak R^{\mathrm{TV}}_{\mathcal C}(\Delta_{2d};n,d,\varepsilon)
     \ge c\,r_{\mathcal C}(n,d,\varepsilon),\qquad
 \mathfrak H^{\mathrm{TV}}_{\mathcal C}(\Delta_{2d};n,d,\varepsilon)
     \ge c\,h_{\mathcal C}(n,d,\varepsilon).
\]
The second quantity uses connected closed intervals in \([0,1]\) with finite global \(0.90\) coverage on all of \(\Delta_{2d}\). The target is \(D_{\mathrm{TV}}(\mathsf p)=\operatorname{TV}(\mathsf p,\mathsf U_{2d})\). The bounds cover arbitrary public seeds, nonidentical kernels, standard-Borel messages and sequential histories. This corollary makes only a lower-bound claim for the full simplex; no matching full-simplex upper is asserted.

items.label: Cited result lem:bernstein-absolute-approximation-limit
items.nl: For \(e_K=\inf_{\deg p\le K}\sup_{|x|\le1}|p(x)-|x||\), the limit along positive even integers is \(\lim_{K\to\infty}K e_K=\beta_*\), where \(0.278<\beta_*<0.286\).
